newsitem.title: USA: Laser EpiTouch gets FDA nod to remove hair.
newsitem.headline: Laser EpiTouch gets FDA nod to remove hair.

text.p: Israel's Laser Industries Ltd said on Tuesday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted marketing clearance to its hair removal technology, which is the subject of a patent dispute.

Laser Industries said it received notification on March 7 that its EpiTouch ruby laser was granted marketing clearance for hair removal. EpiTouch would be sold in the United States through Sharplan 2000 Inc, a joint venture between Laser Industries and MEHL/Biophile International Corp.
MEHL/Biophile owned the technology and licensed it to Sharplan 2000, Sharplan president Michel Kochman said.
But Palomar Medical Technologies Inc said on Monday it held exclusive worldwide license for the technology, which it said was developed at Massachusetts General Hospital.
Earlier Tuesday, Palomar said it was issued a U.S. patent protecting its laser-based hair removal technology called EpiLaser, which received FDA marketing clearance Monday.
MEHL/Biophile had announced on Monday it filed suit against Palomar seeking to prevent Palomar from marketing its laser hair removal products in the United States.

MEHL/Biophile contends Palomar infringed on a patented method of laser hair removal it held exclusive license for and alleged Palomar marketed its product before receiving FDA clearance. Palomar denied these allegations.
The EpiTouch is a dual mode system which also treats tattoos and pigmented lesions, Laser Industries said.
It was the only ruby laser to offer this dual treatment mode, the company said.

Laser Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Benjamin Givli said: "FDA clearance of the EpiTouch Laser is a significant step in our effort to grow the consumer and physician market for laser hair removal."
